html:
The siege of Melos took place in 416 BCE, when Athens attacked the small Aegean island of Melos during the Peloponnesian War.

The Melians were Dorians with old ties to Sparta, but they had stayed neutral. Athens wanted every island in its empire, the Delian League. Its envoys demanded that Melos submit and pay tribute or be destroyed. The Melians refused and were besieged through the winter. When the city fell, the Athenians killed the grown men and sold the women and children as slaves. Five hundred Athenian settlers took over the island.

Thucydides turned the talks into the Melian Dialogue, one of the most read passages in all history. The Athenians say that justice only applies between equals, and that "the strong do what they can and the weak suffer what they must". The Melians appeal to fairness and hope, and lose everything. Ten years earlier Athens had spared the rebels of Mytilene; at Melos it did not. After the war Lysander brought the surviving Melians home.
sum: The siege of Melos took place in 416 BCE, when Athens attacked the small Aegean island of Melos during the Peloponnesian War.
